issue_context.title: Feature Request: IgnoreNullProperties switch on ConvertTo-Json
issue_context.body:
# Summary of the new feature/enhancement

Many REST API that consume JSON don't accept null values, and sometimes when dealing with PowerShell objects this is easier said than done, especially if you're using pre-build .NET stuff. It would be nice if there was a switch parameter on the cmdlet to ignore properties with null values in the JSON string output. 

# Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

I currently have a solution for this from [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33038848/how-to-exclude-non-valued-object-properties-when-converting-to-json-in-powershel) thread, but I imagine I'm not the only with this issue, so this could be a nice solution. Given any PowerShell Object:

    $PowerShellObject | ForEach-Object {

        $NonEmptyProperties = $_.psobject.Properties | Where-Object {$null -ne $_.Value} | Select- 
       Object -ExpandProperty Name

        # Convert object to JSON with only non-empty properties
        $_ | Select-Object -Property $NonEmptyProperties | ConvertTo-Json
    }

I've been taking a look at this, and it doesn't seem like setting the NullValueHandling alone catches all nulls. For example, the following:
```
$object = @{
  NotNullProperty = "not-null",
  NullProperty = $null
}
```
serializes to:
```
{
  "NotNullProperty": "not-null",
  "NullProperty": null
}
```

I'm not sure if there's a bug in what I've written so far, or if LanguagePrimitives.IsNullLike should be involved somehow? Is there some other way of checking for $null (and others) that should be used by cmdlets?

@mdalepiane I think you may want to move the null-value check to first thing in the loop there. That way, if you end up with a key that can't be cast to string properly (unlikely, but I suppose it can happen) which _also_ has a null value, it'll be ignored. If the value is null and you're ignoring null values, there's no reason to error out in the case that the key can't be serialized correctly -- even if it could, you'd be skipping it anyway.

review_comments:
After some investigations I think it is not right. https://github.com/JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json/issues/1491
We should not filter out records from arrays and dictionaries if value is null.
We should filter out only __properties__ with null values.

~The same for RemoveNullProperties(). For pure `Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JObject` serializer with `jsonSettings.NullValueHandling = NullValueHandling.Ignore` will do all work~ - it is conversion, not serialization. :-(

I guess all that we should do in the PR is only to filter out PSObject properties with null values.
Looking at the issue you mentioned it seems that the Newtonsoft behavior is by design and not a bug at all. But should it work this way? Why?
Core behavior is the same. I think we should follow Newtonsoft and Core.

Let me see if I got it right: what keeps the serializer `NullValueHandling.Ignore` from working properly is the fact that we convert everything into dictionaries and for dictionaries and arrays the behavior is to always keep nulls.

So we need the workaround for types that were not originally dicts or arrays: JObject, PSObject and CustomObject. Maybe we don't need it at all for JObject, I'm not sure why it was being converted into a dict in the first place.

Yes, you got it right. I guess it come from limitations of old Core APIs. MSFT team used Newtonsoft library but custom serialization at porting time. (Perhaps it is not easy to implement a converter on Newtonsoft.Json).
In last days I found that .Net Core 3.0 has new power Json API and started working on porting  ConvertFrom-Json from Netonsoft.Json to Core. After some experiments I had to switch to ConvertTo-Json cmdlet. I was supposed to do this work after merging the PR, but now I’m thinking of pulling my PR because it will simplifying the code and adding IgnoreNullValue - I hope it will as simple as adding an option.
Since this will simplify a lot the work I will wait until the port is complete and add IgnoreNullVale in the new code
